authoring_note: Authored inline at the TICKET_PLAN_ARBITER_MODEL (opus) tier rather than by a fresh dispatch. The driver independently holds every premise this plan rests on — the PR #320 diff, DEV-2341's residual ledger, the five-round review history, the verified per-tier trip_date semantics (KitRangePathsQuery:197 vs KitScanPathsQuery's toDate), the three call sites' timezone args, and the injection risk in the R7 fix. A fresh-context arbiter would have had to take all of that on trust. Same call, same reason, as DEV-2222's own plan step.

sizing_gate.reasoning: 4 code files + 3 test files. Code-file count is 4, under the >6 split threshold. One concern: make Kit User Path render scan-only kits correctly. R1 (which kits are eligible), R3 (at what granularity) and R7 (what a 'day' means) are three facets of that single fallback, not separable features — R3 is incorrect without R7, and R1 falls out of R3's design for free.

perf_gate.reasoning: No perf is deferred on a >1B-row ClickHouse surface. The two driving tables were measured directly: clarity.sc_positions is 331,106,659 rows and clarity.kit_scan_paths is 1,680,578 — neither is in the >1B class (contrast hits_cold at ~3.5B). Tier 2 is one batched read on kit_scan_paths' own (org_id, kit_id, timestamp) key prefix, the same access pattern two existing production callers already run, and the plan narrows it further (see t1 step 5).

blast_radius_note: No configured sensitive glob matches (no migrations, billing, Shield/Policies/auth, Clickhouse*Purge|Cleanup, PruneScans), so no formal blast_radius tag. But the R7 fix changes a SHARED query class whose trip_date is consumed by a live Scout surface (ClarityScoutBirdsEyeController:544). That consumer must get explicit test coverage, and Phase 5 must run 3 lanes — this is date-boundary logic, which is a standing 3-lane trigger.

subtasks.title: Kit User Path: per-(kit, local day) kit_scan_paths fallback, incl. mapping-less kits and a timezone-correct day key
subtasks.approach:
Single interlocking change, implemented TDD. Start from PR #320's review-hardened shape (branch claude/dev-2222-cf9a90) as prior art rebased onto current main, then layer R1, R3 and R7 on top. Ordered steps:

1. ClickhouseQuery::buildCacheKey(): private -> protected (both cachedHandle()s need it).

2. KitRangePathsQuery::cachedHandle() and KitScanPathsQuery::cachedHandle(): port verbatim from PR #320 — same 5-minute cache-key shape as query(cache:true), 3s TTL under admin_impersonator, but wrapping handle() so exceptions PROPAGATE instead of being swallowed to []. This is R2, already ratified and landed on #320.

3. R7 — KitScanPathsQuery day key. Replace `toString(toDate(timestamp)) AS trip_date` with a timezone-aware `toString(toDate(timestamp, '<tz>'))`, using the $timezone all three call sites already pass. SECURITY: $timezone resolves from $user->timezone -> $this->dti['timeZone'] (user-influenced JSON) and would now be interpolated into raw SQL, so it MUST first go through a timezone_identifiers_list() whitelist — mirror KitRangePathsQuery::safeTimezone() rather than inventing a new guard. The class already addslashes()es $layer, so treating these args as untrusted is established precedent here.

4. R1 — eligible kit set. In KitUserPathController::paths(), keep kitsByMapping() for the tier-1 mapping list but ALSO key the full Kit collection by id ($byId). Replace the `if ($byMapping === []) return response()->json([])` early return with a no-kits-at-all check, and make tier 1 run only when $mappings !== [] so a purely mapping-less selection skips straight to tier 2. This mirrors ClarityScoutBirdsEyeController::driverPositions(), which does exactly this on purpose with a warning comment at :175-177, and it stops porting the anti-pattern okf/concepts/scout-clickhouse-queries.md:141 warns against.

5. R3 — per-(kit, day) granularity, replacing the whole-window per-kit set-difference. Build covered[kit_id][YYYY-MM-DD] from tier-1 segments (resolving mapping -> Kit via $byMapping; trip_date is already viewer-local on tier 1). Enumerate the window's local days from the same $localStart/$localEnd used for the tier-2 bounds. Skip any kit whose covered-day count already spans every window day — this preserves PR #320's allocation property that a GPS-healthy org issues NO tier-2 read at all. Then ONE batched KitScanPathsQuery::cachedHandle() for the remaining kit ids, and drop any returned row whose (kit_id, trip_date) tier 1 already renders. R1 falls out for free: a mapping-less kit has no tier-1 coverage, so all of its days fall back.

6. Keep every settled decision from PR #320's five review rounds intact: $localStart/$localEnd captured BEFORE Carbon::utc() mutates in place; tier-1 outage -> 503 while a genuine over-budget count stays 422; tier-2 rows accumulated locally and merged only after the loop; a tier-2 failure degrades to tier-1-only and never wipes kits that ARE rendering; tier 2 deliberately outside MAX_RENDER_POINTS; name/color from the resolved Kit, never the CH row; the CH-decoded path json_encode()'d once rather than spliced like tier-1's pre-encoded path_json. Do NOT reintroduce the 'counted points but zero segments' guard — countPoints() counts PRE-SPLIT and <2-point segments are dropped, so that shape is legitimate and common; it was reverted on DEV-2222 for exactly this and a pin test exists.

7. Residual cleanups that were repeat review scorers: R6 — harden scanPathRow() so a false from json_encode($path) cannot emit structurally invalid JSON. R4 — strengthen or drop the near-tautological fallback name/color test. Plus RN5's two mediums: the TTL fork and the vacuous tier-2 test. And document the ratified out-of-scope boundary for ClarityScoutBirdsEyeController::historicalContinuousPaths() where a review lane will read it.

dag_note: ONE node, so Phase 4 takes the single-node fast path in REPO_PATH with no worktree fan-out. The seven files interlock tightly — the controller's R3 diff is only correct once KitScanPathsQuery's day key is timezone-aware, and both cachedHandle()s depend on the ClickhouseQuery visibility widening — so any per-file split would serialize on depends_on anyway while adding worktree and merge risk for no parallelism. test_filter is a real null: the worker runs the full suite command, and the driver additionally runs the shared-class co-callers (Bird's Eye, Scout Map) as the blast-radius check.
